Psilocybin..a game changer

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Psilocybin - a game chaner.

Unique Selling Point:
New Research has indicated the severe depression and anxiety can be successfully treated with "magic" mushroom!Shamans around the world have used hallucinogenics (including psilocybin – magic mushrooms) for millennia to induce a lens into spiritual worlds from where they say they derive their wisdom; in rites of passage; and to treat people’s psychological or spiritual needs. These medicine men are what priests and psychiatrists are in Western society.


Summary:
5 years ago we told the story of then 70 year old Monica Kromhout who held mushroom ceremonies at her home in Somerset West. 15 people at a time would gather at her home.She created the environment for people to experience spiritual enlightenment caused by a “trip” on psilobyn. Participants found that these experiences changed their lives. They became better version of themselves, they gained better insight into themselves and were able to deal better with the challenges in their lives. For some, it helped with addictions they suffered.

Monica was arrested. After her release she continued holding these ceremonies. Then rearrested. Her case is going to the high court and she is being represented her for free is top attorney Paul -Michael Keichel – who was behind the decriminalisation of cannabis. He will argue that her arrest was unconstitutional and that the prohibition of this drug owes its existence to outdated and unfounded convictions on the harmlessness and dependence producing effects of psilocybin motivated by govts with questionable political agendas.

His aim is to decriminalise the use of psilocybin (magic mushrooms) for reactionary and therapeutic purposes.

It's only a matter of time he thinks, that laws around the world will be relaxed in order that psilobyn should be used to treat patients with depression, anxiety, Ptsd. He will present leading research.

Further information:
New trials (Imperial College) in the UK have shown the drug psilocybin to be highly effective in treating depression, Some researchers say it could become ‘indefensible’ to ignore the evidence – but how would it work as a reliable treatment?

Dr Nutt who was involved has been approached to provide an interview and give the science on how psilocybin works on the brain.

It's believed that it's a matter of time before the UK legalises for therapeutic treatments. And just two months ago Oregon became the first state in the USA to legalize the active ingredient in so-called magic mushrooms on an election night that saw more states ease restrictions on drugs across the country.

Some therapist privately use psilobyn to treat patients but they wont come onto the program, as they may lose their license. But there is a website called Phatisa is for professionals in the medical field – a platform to build knowledge to support responsible advancements in the treatment of people with hallucinogens and explore this new medical approach in South Africa.
Leonie Joubert is a cape town award winning science journalist who has a special interest in magic mushrooms, and has created a website to describe the experience, provide research and she also has a pod cast. She is amazing.

Finally, Monica because of lock down now holds Zoom ceremonies and participants all from all over then world. 187 people who have been through the experience at Monica's home have provided supporting affidavit for court.
We need to have a SA psychiatrist on the program as well – what does he think of Monic'a's zoom meetings, are there dangers, who should not use mushrooms, is there ever a bad trip? Or rather a difficult trip. Have there been any deaths.

Finally we need to speak to 2 people who have been on trips.

Script
Monica Cromhout , was not impressed when she was told in court that charges against her were being dropped

Monica: what. You have lost my file, make another one, you have put me through all this trouble, to tell me that you have lost my file

She wanted her day in court and so the state obliged, and a new docket was opened. She had been charged with the possession of and dealing in psilocybin, commonly known as magic mudrooms... a banned substance in South Afirca, which she supplied to participants at at gathering - she calls them Soma Ceremonies - the spirt of the mushroom.
Link: Monica is no stranger to Carte Blanche, we first featured in 2015,
soon after she was arrested during one of her magic mushroom ceremonies in the middle of the night.
An elderly retired professor had became confused at one of her ceremonies and slipped away. Monica and a search team frantically searched for him, , but he had ended up a the police station. The next moment .a contingent of police raided onMonica's house ,confiscated 2 k's psilocybin and locked her up After getting bail, Monica coninuted with these ceremonies in an act of civil disobedience

She claims that over 2000 people from all walks of life, including doctors and attorneys HAVE attend her gatherings Each participants injest a large dosage of psilcyn, 5 grams - and undergo several hours of a deep psychedelic state. Then follow a reported profound sense of enlightenment.

Link: These ceremonies are in tended for spiritual connections but Monica's research has found that participants report positive changes in their lafter taking psilocybin.

Award winning sicience writer and journalist leonie Jnoubert, who suffered depression, claims that psilocybin combined with traditional therapy has had a beneficial impact on her life.



Lione: I have used psilocybin to manage my own mental well being, for 6 years now, very small does occasionally, and occasional these large therapeutic does, and I would say its been life changin... I have become much more empathetic with people, I have been able to understand other people's experiences in relation to my own, and that has allowed for much deeper interpersonal connections
Leonie has released a serialized audio-book, The Psychonauts, which draws together stories from the psilocybin users and it explores the opportunity for psilocybin-assisted therapy in South Africa.

Cape Town psychiatrist, Dr Kevin Stollof, is not surprised by the surge of interest in psilocybin.

Dr Stollof: The reason for that is people are generally quite pessimistic and tired of the limitations of psychiatric medicine, a quarter of people don't respond to anti-depressants, these psychedelic medicines work on different routes or mechanisms which act in a very different way to psychiatric medication.

Brain imaging shows that psychedelics such a s lsd and psilobyn result in different parts of the brain connecting, which can result in deep insights.

Dr Stollof: In doing that, there is something about pathways opening, which has been shut off, and negative pathways or negative thinking patterns, like pathways in the brain, can be dusted over, like filed with snow - and allow a fresh slate on which to form new experiences and think in a different way.


Link: Monica was arrested again in 2017 for the same alleged offence, but she is not taking this lying down - she managed to get a stay in prosecution and is suing the state believing that her constitutional rights were violated.

Monica wants the hight court to legalise or at least decriminalize psilocybin. if she fails there, her attorney paul Michael Keichel, best known for his part in decriminalising the private use of cannabis in SA will petition the constitutional court.

Derek: she is quite a determined lady?

Paul-Michael: She certainly knows what is right, to take on the state to achieve an elevated state of consciousness;

Kietchal for example will argue that it terms of section 12 of the constitution people ought to have a right to put what ever they want into their bodies so long as they are not harming others or placing an undue burden on the state health services.

In their plea plea the state says that it has an obligation to protect all its citizen against harmful substances and it has the support of a SA professor of Paramaceutics who in his affidavit said that the body if evidence currently available for psilocy shows that its not a safe substance for human use.

But there appears to be no confirmed reports of deaths, globally, that are attributed exclusively to psilocybin use  in healthy individuals, although psychiatrists warn that when mixed with other drugs it can lead to psychosis and self harming behaviour . Dr Stollof stressed that certain people should never use it.

Dr Stollof: Those who had had a psychosis before, from being bi-poplar, even psychosis from cannabis usage, if you family members have schizophrenia,


Derek: are you going to introduce the latest research?
Kierchel: ; Absolutely Derek, then world is waking up to psilocybin, for a treatment for a number of psychological ailments.

Kierchel will present a study conducted by the centre of Psychedelic research an Imerpial College in the London.studies that Kierchel will present is will be thr trails that took place recently at the Imperial college in the UK. 12 severally depressed volunteer were treated with psillcybin. Possessor David Nutt is the director of the Neurological iunit at Imperial College

Prof Nutt: So the first showed that people with resistant depression, they had all failed with anti-depressants, and even traditional therapy, the remarkable thing was out of a single treatment, the power of this approach, one single dosing produces profound improvements in the majority of patients.

Derek: So definite evidence that psillcybin was able to treat treatment resistant depression?

Prof Nut: I twas a remarkable study - one of the most powerful interventions
On treatment resistant depression – certainly the most poweful one had ever seen.

But the effects of lose dosages of psiloccyn tend to wear off after three weeks and now studies will be conducted to see if staggered smaller does can hold off then depression.

Prof Nutt: Just in the same way we have seen the UN and who after 80 years accept that cannabis is a medicine, its almost inevitable that in a few years they will accept psilocybin because the weight of evidence will force them to reevaluate their position.

Dr Tollof does not advocate the use of psilocybin at this stage because it's a banned substance. However he does hope the laws are relaxed in order to allow psilocybin assisted psychotherapy. He also emphasizes the need for holders of sermonies to be competent.

Stollof: What is important is that the providers of these ceremonies
are skilled enough to know when to call for medical assistance.

Monica, in response to Covid 19 is now holding zoom mushroom ceremonies where participants participants join from all over South Africa and the world. Each participant is vetted and provided with protocols.

Monica: we recommend that if a person is journeying for the firt time, we suggest that a family member watch over them, and they can contact us as well via what’s app or then phone;

And during the night Monica and several watchers, all experiences in mushroom journeys are in standby should a participant become agitated. Contact is made by phone or what's app messages. Participants even send messages as well during their trip to describe their journey.

In the meantime Kierchal is confident that Monoca has a strong case which will result in lease the decriminalisation of psilocybin. Monica who is hopeful
Derek: what do you want your legacy to be:

Monica: To leave something good behind:

Derek: A gift to SA

Monica; actually the world!
